ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT — TRACKED CHANGES REDLINE

[STANDARD FORM BASE: Depository Bank Standard Form ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT, v. [Current]]
[COUNTERPARTY DRAFT UNDER REVIEW: Borrower's Proposed Account Control Agreement]
[REVIEWED AGAINST: Internal Playbook — Capital Markets/Secured Finance Practice Group; Executed Credit Agreement dated [ ], as amended]

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement"), dated as of [●] (the "Effective Date"), is entered into among [BORROWER], a [state] corporation (the "Grantor"), [SECURED PARTY], as administrative agent (the "Secured Party"), and [DEPOSITORY BANK], a [state] chartered banking corporation (the "Bank").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, the Grantor has entered into that certain Credit Agreement dated as of [●] (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement") among the Grantor, the lenders party thereto from time to time and the Secured Party;

WHEREAS, the Grantor has opened, or will open, one or more securities accounts, deposit accounts or commodity accounts (each, an "Account") with the Bank identified on Schedule I hereto, to which certain assets of the Grantor are or will be credited;

WHEREAS, under the Credit Agreement, the Grantor has granted to the Secured Party a security interest in the Accounts and their proceeds to secure the Secured Obligations (as defined in the Credit Agreement);

WHEREAS, the Secured Party, the Grantor and the Bank desire to enter into this Agreement to perfect and protect the security interest in the Accounts pursuant to Article 8 or Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the Relevant Jurisdiction;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained, the parties agree as follows:

*** REDLINE MARKUP — DELETIONS SHOWN AS STRIKETHROUGH; INSERTIONS SHOWN AS UNDERLINE ***

ARTICLE I
DEFINITIONS

Section 1.1. Defined Terms. As used in this Agreement:

"Account" has the meaning specified in the recitals ~~and means any account listed on Schedule I as may be modified from time to time~~.

INSERT (Playbook §2.1): "Account" means any of the accounts listed on Schedule I hereto, together with all sub-accounts thereunder, and any replacement or successor account established pursuant to Section [4.2]; provided that no account may be added, substituted, or replaced except with the prior written consent of the Secured Party.

"Account Holder" means the Grantor with respect to each Account.

"Agreement" has the meaning specified in the preamble.

"Authorized Person" means each individual designated in writing by the Secured Party to the Bank as authorized to give Entitlement Orders (as defined below) or instructions with respect to the Accounts. The Bank may rely conclusively upon~~any~~ a written notice of the Secured Party designating Authorized Persons ~~and~~ ~~shall have no duty to verify the authority of the Secured Party~~.

INSERT (Playbook §2.3): "Authorized Person" includes any person designated by the Secured Party from time to time in a signed written notice delivered to the Bank, and the Bank shall not be obligated to verify the authority of the Secured Party or any Authorized Person to act on behalf of the Secured Party beyond receipt of such written notice.

"Bank" has the meaning specified in the preamble.

"Commodity Account" has the meaning specified in Section 9-106 of the UCC.

"Control" has the meaning specified in Section 8-106 of the UCC with respect to security entitlements and Section 9-106 or 9-104 of the UCC with respect to deposit accounts and commodity accounts, as applicable.

"Deposit Account" has the meaning specified in Section 9-102(a)(29) of the UCC.

"Entitlement Order" means a notification communicated to the Bank directing the transfer or redemption of a financial asset to which the Secured Party has control under the UCC.

INSERT (Playbook §2.4): "Entitlement Order" shall also include any instruction directing disposition of funds or securities in the Account, whether denominated as an entitlement order, instruction, or otherwise, and shall include direction of payment to the Secured Party or its designee.

"Event of Default" has the meaning specified in the Credit Agreement.

INSERT (Playbook §2.5): "Financial Asset" has the meaning specified in Section 8-102(a)(9) of the UCC and includes any security, including a certificated or uncertificated security, any obligation of a person or entity, and any property (including any investment property or commodity contract) that is held by the Bank in the Account.

"Grantor" has the meaning specified in the preamble.

"Investment Property" has the meaning specified in Section 9-102(a)(49) of the UCC.

"No-Action Instruction" means written notice by the Secured Party to the Bank that the Secured Party no longer consents to the Grantor's ability to exercise any rights with respect to the Accounts.

"Proceeds" has the meaning specified in Section 9-102(a)(64) of the UCC.

"Secured Obligations" means the "Obligations" as defined in the Credit Agreement, including all obligations of the Grantor arising under any Swap Contracts, Cash Management Agreements, and other documents executed in connection with the Credit Agreement.

"Secured Party" has the meaning specified in the preamble.

"Securities Account" has the meaning specified in Section 8-501 of the UCC.

INSERT (Playbook §2.6): "Securities Intermediary" means the Bank, solely in its capacity as the securities intermediary with respect to the relevant Securities Accounts.

"UCC" means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the Relevant Jurisdiction from time to time.

"Relevant Jurisdiction" means the State of [●] with respect to each relevant matter governed by the UCC.

Section 1.2. ~~Rules of Construction.~~ Terms used but not defined herein that are defined in the Credit Agreement ~~shall~~ have ~~the meanings~~ assigned therein, unless the context otherwise requires. The rules of construction in the Credit Agreement apply to this Agreement mutatis mutandis.

ARTICLE II
REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

Section 2.1. Representations and Warranties of the Grantor. The Grantor represents and warrants to the Secured Party that:

(a) The Grantor ~~holds~~ is the sole legal and beneficial owner of the Accounts and the assets credited thereto, free and clear of all ~~liens~~ (except the security interest created under this Agreement), claims, ~~encumbrances~~ and other rights of third parties whatsoever.

INSERT (Playbook §3.1): The Grantor is the sole legal and beneficial owner of all Financial Assets, funds, and other property credited to the Accounts, and the Grantor has not pledged, assigned, or otherwise encumbered the Accounts or any property credited thereto, except in favor of the Secured Party.

(b) The Grantor has full power and authority to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement and to grant the security interest described herein.

(c) ~~The execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement do not~~~ conflict with or constitute a breach of any provision of ~~the Grantor's organizational documents or any agreement to which the Grantor is a party.~~

INSERT (Playbook §3.2): The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement will not (i) violate any provision of any law, rule, regulation, order, writ, judgment, injunction, decree, determination or award presently in effect having applicability to the Grantor, (ii) violate or result in a default under the constituent documents of the Grantor, (iii) violate or result in a default under any material agreement binding on the Grantor or any of its properties, or (iv) result in the creation or imposition of any lien on any of the assets of the Grantor other than the security interest contemplated by this Agreement.

(d) The Grantor has ~~obtained all approvals~~ ~~consents and authorizations~~ necessary for its execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement.

INSERT (Playbook §3.3): All consents, approvals, authorizations, filings, or notices required for the valid execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been or will be obtained or made, and are in full force and effect.

(e) ~~The Account is a securities account, deposit account, or commodity account~~ ~~maintained~~ with the Bank within the meaning of the UCC.

INSERT (Playbook §3.4): Each Account (i) is a securities account, deposit account, or commodity account, as applicable, maintained by the Bank for the Grantor, (ii) is identified in the Bank's records by account number and title as set forth on Schedule I, and (iii) is in the name of the Grantor.

(f) ~~No Account is subject to any subordination agreement or similar arrangement.~~

INSERT (Playbook §3.5): No person other than the Grantor and the Secured Party has any right, title, or interest in or to the Accounts or any property credited thereto, and no Account is subject to any other control agreement, custodial agreement, or similar arrangement in favor of any other person.

(g) The Grantor represents that each Account is maintained with the Bank in the Relevant Jurisdiction.

Section 2.2. Representations and Warranties of the Bank. The Bank represents and warrants to the Secured Party that:

(a) The Bank is a [state] chartered banking corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of [●], and has full corporate power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement.

(b) The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with the Bank's organizational documents, any law, rule, or regulation, or any contract to which the Bank is a party, and require no governmental approvals (or such approvals have been obtained).

(c) The Bank ~~maintains~~ the Accounts ~~as securities accounts, deposit accounts, or commodity accounts~~ ~~respectively~~ in its ordinary course of business, and the Account numbers, titles, and types set forth on Schedule I are accurate.

INSERT (Playbook §3.7): Each Account is and will remain a "securities account," "deposit account," or "commodity account" within the meaning of the UCC, as applicable. The Bank has not received notice of, and does not maintain, any setoff right, bankers' lien, or other claim to the Accounts or property credited thereto other than in favor of the Secured Party.

(d) The Bank has not entered into and will not enter into any other agreement with any person relating to the Accounts or any property credited thereto that could conflict with the Secured Party's rights under this Agreement.

INSERT (Playbook §3.8): The Bank shall not, without the prior written consent of the Secured Party, agree to comply with entitlement orders or instructions from any person other than the Secured Party and its Authorized Persons with respect to the Accounts, and the Bank shall notify the Secured Party promptly upon receiving any such instruction or order from any other person.

(e) ~~The Bank maintains records identifying the Grantor as the entitlement holder of each Account.~~

INSERT (Playbook §3.9): The Bank maintains records identifying the Grantor as the entitlement holder of each Securities Account, the account holder of each Deposit Account, and the commodity customer of each Commodity Account, as applicable, and such records are sufficient to establish the Secured Party's control upon compliance with the terms of this Agreement.

Section 2.3. ~~Representations and Warranties~~ ~~of~~ ~~the Secured Party.~~ The Secured Party represents and warrants that it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of [●] and has full power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement.

ARTICLE III
COVENANTS OF THE BANK

Section 3.1. ~~Compliance with Instructions.~~ The Bank shall comply with all Entitlement Orders and other instructions originated by the Secured Party or any Authorized Person without further consent by the Grantor.

INSERT (Playbook §4.1): The Bank shall comply with and act upon any Entitlement Order or other instruction originated by the Secured Party or any Authorized Person directing disposition of the Financial Assets or funds in an Account, without further consent of the Grantor and without any duty to inquire into or verify the circumstances or the adequacy of consideration for such instruction.

Section 3.2. ~~No Prior Notice.~~ The Grantor ~~waives~~ any requirement that the Secured Party provide prior notice to the Grantor before delivering Entitlement Orders to the Bank, and the Bank may act on such orders without notice to the Grantor.

INSERT (Playbook §4.2): The Grantor and the Bank acknowledge that the Secured Party may deliver Entitlement Orders or instructions to the Bank at any time, effective immediately, without prior notice to or consent of the Grantor. The Bank shall act upon such orders and instructions promptly and in accordance with the terms of this Agreement.

Section 3.3. Control. The Bank acknowledges and agrees that the Secured Party has Control over the Accounts and all related property, including the exclusive right to direct the disposition of funds and Financial Assets pursuant to this Agreement.

INSERT (Playbook §4.3): The Bank agrees that, upon execution of this Agreement, the Secured Party shall have Control over each Account and all Financial Assets, funds, and property credited thereto, with the exclusive right to direct the disposition thereof, including the right to cause the transfer or redemption of Financial Assets and the disposition of funds.

Section 3.4. ~~Statements and Confirmations.~~ The Bank shall send, or make available, to the Secured Party copies of statements and confirmations for each Account at such times as are provided under the applicable account agreement, ~~and in no event less frequently than monthly~~.

INSERT (Playbook §4.4): The Bank shall provide the Secured Party with monthly statements for each Account, and shall make available an electronic view or download of transaction activity in each Account upon request, at no cost to the Secured Party. The Bank shall also provide the Secured Party with prompt notice (no later than two (2) business days after the Bank obtains actual knowledge) of any unauthorized transaction or attempted transaction in any Account.

Section 3.5. Change of Account Number. The Bank shall not change the number of any Account, or close or terminate any Account, without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.

INSERT (Playbook §4.5): In the event of a change in the account number of any Account (including due to a merger, acquisition, or system migration), the Bank shall promptly (within three (3) business days) provide written notice to the Secured Party of the new account number, and such replacement account shall automatically be subject to this Agreement without further action by any party.

Section 3.6. ~~Additional Accounts.~~ ~~The Grantor shall~~ ~~maintain~~ ~~all of~~ its ~~securities accounts, deposit accounts, and commodity accounts~~ ~~with~~ ~~the Bank~~.

INSERT (Playbook §4.6): The Grantor shall not open or maintain any additional securities account, deposit account, or commodity account with the Bank or any other financial institution without the prior written consent of the Secured Party, unless such account is subject to a control agreement in favor of the Secured Party in the form and substance required by the Secured Party.

Section 3.7. Waiver of Setoff and Liens. The Bank waives any right of setoff, banker's lien, or other similar right with respect to the Accounts.

INSERT (Playbook §4.7): The Bank irrevocably and unconditionally waives any right of setoff, banker's lien, security interest, or other claim (including any right of recoupment) that the Bank may have against any Account or any property credited thereto, whether arising by operation of law, contract, or otherwise; provided, however, that the Bank retains its right to deduct customary fees and service charges for maintaining the Accounts in accordance with the applicable account agreements.

Section 3.8. ~~Third-Party Instructions.~~ ~~The Bank shall not~~ ~~comply with~~ ~~any~~ ~~instructions~~ ~~or entitlement orders~~ ~~from any person other than~~ ~~the Secured Party~~ ~~or its Authorized Persons~~.

INSERT (Playbook §4.8): The Bank shall comply exclusively with instructions and entitlement orders originated by the Secured Party or its Authorized Persons with respect to the Accounts, and shall not comply with any instruction or entitlement order from the Grantor, any receiver, trustee, or other third party with respect to the Accounts, unless such instruction or order is (i) accompanied by the prior written consent of the Secured Party, or (ii) issued by a court of competent jurisdiction.

Section 3.9. Available Balance. The Bank shall ~~calculate~~ ~~the available balance~~ of each Deposit Account ~~on a daily basis~~.

INSERT (Playbook §4.9): The Bank shall, on each business day, calculate and make available to the Secured Party the available balance of each Deposit Account, including any amounts available under any sweep or investment arrangement, and shall provide prompt notice to the Secured Party of the available balance upon request.

Section 3.10. Compliance with Court Orders. The Bank shall promptly notify the Secured Party upon receiving any court order, judgment, garnishment, attachment, or other legal process affecting or seeking to affect any Account.

INSERT (Playbook §4.10): The Bank shall notify the Secured Party within two (2) business days of receiving any such legal process, shall provide the Secured Party with a copy of such process upon request, and shall not comply with any such process that purports to direct disposition of Financial Assets in a Securities Account unless such process is enforceable against the property under applicable law and the Bank is legally compelled to comply.

ARTICLE IV
ACCOUNT DETAILS AND MAINTENANCE

Section 4.1. Schedule I. The Accounts subject to this Agreement and the applicable account details are set forth on Schedule I, which shall be deemed amended by the Bank and the Secured Party from time to time by written notice.

INSERT (Playbook §5.1): Schedule I shall set forth with respect to each Account: (i) the account number, (ii) the account title, (iii) the account type (i.e., securities, deposit, or commodity), (iv) the branch or office at which the Account is maintained, (v) the name of the entitlement holder or account holder, as applicable, and (vi) any applicable sub-accounts. The Bank shall confirm the accuracy of Schedule I in writing upon execution of this Agreement and within five (5) business days after any change to the Account details.

Section 4.2. ~~New Accounts.~~ The Grantor may establish additional Accounts subject to this Agreement with the written consent of the Secured Party, which consent may be granted or withheld in the Secured Party's sole discretion.

INSERT (Playbook §5.2): Any additional account created by the Grantor with the Bank that is designated in a written notice from the Secured Party shall automatically become an Account under this Agreement upon the Bank's receipt of such notice, without the need for execution of a new agreement or amendment. The Bank shall confirm in writing the receipt and effectiveness of such notice within three (3) business days.

Section 4.3. Account Closure. The Bank shall not close any Account without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.

INSERT (Playbook §5.3): If the Bank determines it is required to close any Account for legal, regulatory, or compliance reasons, the Bank shall provide the Secured Party with at least ten (10) days' prior written notice, shall cooperate with the Secured Party to establish a replacement Account subject to this Agreement, and shall not transfer amounts out of the closed Account except to such replacement Account or as otherwise directed by the Secured Party.

ARTICLE V
EVENTS OF DEFAULT AND REMEDIES

Section 5.1. ~~Rights Upon Default.~~ Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, the Secured Party may direct the Bank to:

(a) transfer or cause to be transferred any or all Financial Assets or funds from any Account to an account designated by the Secured Party;

(b) sell, liquidate, or redeem any or all Financial Assets in the Accounts, and apply the proceeds to the Secured Obligations;

(c) execute such documents and take such actions as the Secured Party deems necessary or appropriate to effectuate the foregoing, without any further consent from the Grantor.

INSERT (Playbook §6.1): Following the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, the Secured Party may direct the Bank to take any of the foregoing actions without notice to, or consent of, the Grantor. The Bank shall comply with such directions promptly, and shall not require the Grantor's signature, endorsement, or confirmation for any transfer, sale, or disposition. The Bank shall not be liable for any loss, cost, or expense incurred as a result of acting on the Secured Party's directions in accordance with this Section.

Section 5.2. ~~Application of Proceeds.~~ The Secured Party shall apply all proceeds received under this Agreement to the Secured Obligations in accordance with the Credit Agreement.

Section 5.3. ~~Grantor's Waiver of Notice.~~ The Grantor ~~waives~~ ~~any right to notice~~ ~~prior to~~ ~~any~~ action taken by the Secured Party or the Bank under this Article.

INSERT (Playbook §6.2): The Grantor irrevocably waives any right to receive notice prior to any action taken by the Secured Party or the Bank under this Agreement, including any notice of sale, disposition, or transfer of the Financial Assets or funds, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.

ARTICLE VI
INDEMNITY

Section 6.1. ~~Indemnification~~ by ~~the~~ ~~Bank~~. The Bank shall indemnify the Secured Party against any and all losses, claims, damages, and liabilities arising from the Bank's gross negligence or willful misconduct in performing its obligations under this Agreement.

INSERT (Playbook §7.1): The Bank shall indemnify and hold harmless the Secured Party and its officers, directors, employees, agents, and affiliates from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred or suffered by the Secured Party arising out of or in connection with (i) the Bank's failure to comply with any provision of this Agreement, (ii) the Bank's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of this Agreement, (iii) any action taken or omitted to be taken by the Bank in accordance with a court order or direction of a receiver or similar official that results in loss to the Secured Party, or (iv) any claim by the Grantor or any third party relating to actions taken by the Bank in accordance with this Agreement.

Section 6.2. Indemnification by the Grantor. The Grantor shall indemnify the Bank against any losses, claims, damages, and liabilities arising from the Bank's compliance with the instructions of the Secured Party or the Grantor, except to the extent caused by the Bank's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Section 6.3. ~~Indemnification~~ by ~~the~~ ~~Secured Party~~. The Secured Party shall indemnify the Bank against any losses, claims, damages, and liabilities arising from the Bank's compliance with the instructions of the Secured Party, except to the extent such losses arise from the Bank's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

INSERT (Playbook §7.3): The Secured Party's indemnification obligation to the Bank shall not apply to losses arising from the Bank's failure to comply with this Agreement, the Bank's violation of applicable law, or the Bank's compliance with instructions of persons other than the Secured Party or its Authorized Persons.

ARTICLE VII
MISCELLANEOUS

Section 7.1. ~~Notices.~~ All notices and other communications hereunder shall be in writing and delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of the Credit Agreement, or to the parties at their respective addresses set forth on the signature pages hereto.

Section 7.2. Amendments. ~~This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument~~ ~~signed by~~ ~~all parties~~.

INSERT (Playbook §8.2): This Agreement may be amended, modified, or supplemented from time to time by a written instrument executed by each of the Grantor, the Secured Party, and the Bank; provided, however, that Schedule I may be amended by written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank and the Grantor in accordance with Section 4.1.

Section 7.3. ~~Successors and Assigns.~~ This Agreement shall be binding upon and shall inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and permitted assigns.

INSERT (Playbook §8.3): The Secured Party may assign its rights, benefits, and obligations under this Agreement to any successor administrative agent under the Credit Agreement without the consent of the Grantor or the Bank, upon written notice to each of them.

Section 7.4. ~~Governing Law.~~ ~~This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of [●], without regard to its conflict of laws principles.~~

INSERT (Playbook §8.4): This Agreement, and all obligations hereunder, shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, without giving effect to the choice of law provisions thereof; provided, however, that the provisions of this Agreement relating to the perfection and effectiveness of the Secured Party's security interest in each Account (including the grant of Control) shall be governed by the laws of the jurisdiction specified in Section 9-301, 9-304, 9-305, or 9-306 of the UCC, as applicable.

Section 7.5. Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial. Each party hereby submits to the nonexclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the State of [●] and the federal courts located therein, and hereby waives any right to trial by jury in any action or proceeding relating to this Agreement.

INSERT (Playbook §8.5): EACH PARTY HERETO IRREVOCABLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY AGREES THAT ANY LEGAL ACTION OR PROCEEDING ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE BROUGHT IN THE FEDERAL COURTS OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA LOCATED IN THE BOROUGH OF MANHATTAN, NEW YORK, OR THE COURTS OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK LOCATED IN THE COUNTY OF NEW YORK, AND EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY SUBMITS TO THE EXCLUSIVE JURISDICTION OF SUCH COURTS. EACH PARTY HEREBY WAIVES, TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION OR PROCEEDING ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.

Section 7.6. ~~Counterparts.~~ This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.

INSERT (Playbook §8.6): Delivery of an executed counterpart of this Agreement by facsimile or electronic transmission (including PDF) shall be effective as delivery of an original executed counterpart.

Section 7.7. ~~Entire Agreement.~~ This Agreement, together with the Credit Agreement and the other Loan Documents, constitutes the entire agreement among the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof.

Section 7.8. ~~Survival.~~ The provisions of this Agreement, including the Bank's agreements with respect to Control and the Secured Party's security interest in the Accounts, shall survive the termination of the Credit Agreement until such time as all Secured Obligations have been indefeasibly paid in full and the Secured Party has released its security interest in the Accounts.

INSERT (Playbook §8.8): This Agreement shall remain in full force and effect until (i) the Secured Obligations have been indefeasibly paid in full in cash, (ii) all commitments under the Credit Agreement have been terminated, and (iii) the Secured Party has delivered to the Bank a written release confirming the termination of this Agreement and directing the Bank to comply with the instructions of the Grantor.

Section 7.9. ~~Severability~~ and ~~Invalidity~~. If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

Section 7.10. ~~No Waiver.~~ ~~No failure or delay~~ by any party in exercising any right under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof.

Section 7.11. ~~Bank's~~ ~~Right~~ ~~to~~ ~~Rely~~ ~~on~~ ~~Instructions~~. The Bank shall be entitled to rely conclusively upon, and shall incur no liability for acting in accordance with, any instruction, notice, or Entitlement Order reasonably believed by it to be genuine and signed or presented by the Secured Party or an Authorized Person.

Section 7.12. ~~Confidentiality~~. The Bank shall keep confidential and shall not disclose to any person (other than the Grantor and the Secured Party) any information regarding the Accounts, the Grantor, or the transactions contemplated hereby, except (a) as required by law, regulation, or court order, or (b) as necessary to perform its obligations under this Agreement.

Section 7.13. ~~Costs and Expenses~~. The Grantor shall reimburse the Secured Party for all reasonable costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by the Secured Party in connection with the preparation, negotiation, execution, enforcement, or termination of this Agreement.

MEMORANDUM

TO: Client — Credit Committee
FROM: Law Firm Company — Secured Finance & Capital Markets Group
DATE: [●]
RE: Issues and Risk Memorandum — Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement (ACA)

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement (the "Draft ACA") against (i) our firm's internal playbook for account control agreements in secured lending transactions (the "Playbook"), (ii) the executed Credit Agreement (the "Credit Agreement"), (iii) the Depository Bank's standard form account control agreement (the "Bank Form"), (iv) the account details applicable to the collateral accounts, and (v) the related correspondence and closing checklists exchanged among counsel for the parties.

The Draft ACA deviates materially from the Bank Form and the Playbook in a number of respects. While some deviations reflect acceptable commercial compromise, others create substantive risk to the perfection and priority of the Secured Party's security interest in the collateral accounts. In particular, the counterparty's Draft ACA dilutes the Secured Party's control rights, narrows the scope of the accounts and assets subject to the security interest, adds restrictive conditions on the exercise of remedies, and includes indemnification and liability carve-outs that are off-market.

We have prepared a tracked-changes redline (the "Redline") reflecting all required modifications and insertions. This memorandum identifies, with section references, every deviation, missing protection, and off-market term; assesses the associated risk; quantifies exposure where feasible; and sets forth our recommended negotiating positions.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

II. SOURCE DOCUMENTS AND COMPARISON BASELINE

The review was conducted against the following benchmarks:

A. Internal Playbook — Account Control Agreement Standards
The Firm's Playbook for ACAs in secured credit facilities requires, among other things:
- Unconditional Control for the Secured Party over all collateral accounts (UCC §§ 8-106, 9-104, 9-106);
- Compliance by the Bank with entitlement orders from the Secured Party without further consent of the Grantor;
- Broad definition of "Account" and "Financial Asset" to capture all property credited to the accounts;
- Ongoing account maintenance obligations and notice requirements on the Bank;
- Waiver of setoff, banker's lien, and similar rights by the Bank;
- Indemnification by the Bank for failure to comply with the Agreement, gross negligence, and willful misconduct;
- New York governing law and exclusive New York forum, with jury trial waiver;
- Automatic successorship for any replacement administrative agent;
- Survival of the Agreement until indefeasible payment and termination by written release.

B. Executed Credit Agreement
The Credit Agreement requires that the Secured Party obtain "control" (as defined in the UCC) over all deposit, securities, and commodity accounts of the Grantor within 30 days after the Closing Date. The Credit Agreement defines the "Obligations" to include term loans, revolving loans, letters of credit, swap obligations, and cash management obligations.

C. Depository Bank's Standard Form ACA
The Bank Form serves as the baseline document from which the counterparty's Draft ACA was derived. The Bank Form reflects market-standard provisions consistent with the Playbook.

D. Account Details
The Accounts subject to the ACA include securities accounts, deposit accounts, and commodity accounts maintained with the Bank, as set forth on Schedule I to the Draft ACA.

E. Related Correspondence and Checklists
The parties' correspondence reflects that the counterparty sought to (i) narrow the scope of the security interest, (ii) require notice and consent rights for the Grantor, (iii) cap the Bank's liability, and (iv) impose setoff preservation rights for the Bank.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

III. DETAILED DEVIATION AND RISK ANALYSIS

The following is a section-by-section analysis of each deviation, missing protection, and off-market term identified in the Draft ACA.

───

A. SECTION 1.1 — DEFINITIONS

Deviation 1: Definition of "Account" — Narrowing of Scope
Section Reference: Draft ACA §1.1, "Account"
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §2.1 — "Account" must include all accounts listed on Schedule I plus all sub-accounts, replacement accounts, and successor accounts, and no account may be added, substituted, or replaced without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.
Counterparty Draft: Limits "Account" to accounts "as may be modified from time to time," which would permit unilateral modification by the Grantor and the Bank without the Secured Party's consent. This is a material weakening of the collateral coverage.
Risk Rating: HIGH
Risk Analysis: If the Grantor or the Bank can modify the definition of "Account" unilaterally, the Secured Party's security interest could be unintentionally limited to a subset of the collateral, potentially undermining perfection and priority in accounts transferred or retitled without notice. This creates a gap risk under UCC Article 9 where the account could be moved or retitled to a non-party entity while the Secured Party loses control.
Exposure: Potentially the full value of any accounts removed from coverage. If the collateral accounts secure a $50MM facility, an unprotected transfer of one or more accounts could expose the Secured Party to a significant shortfall upon default.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require the Playbook definition. Acceptable compromise: allow additions by notice from the Secured Party, but provide that any removal or modification of accounts requires the Secured Party's prior written consent.

Deviation 2: Definition of "Authorized Person" — Reduced Formality
Section Reference: Draft ACA §1.1, "Authorized Person"
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §2.3 — Authorized Persons must be designated by written notice from the Secured Party, and the Bank must be permitted to rely conclusively on such notice.
Counterparty Draft: Removes the Bank's "conclusive reliance" protection, which could expose the Bank to inquiries and delays in complying with instructions.
Risk Rating: MODERATE
Risk Analysis: While this deviation affects the Bank's protection more than the Secured Party's, the Bank's reluctance to act without conclusive reliance could create delay risk in the exercise of remedies. The Bank may demand additional verification before acting on the Secured Party's instructions, creating time-of-essence risk in a default scenario.
Exposure: Potential delay in enforcement could allow dissipation of assets or create preference/avoidance issues in an insolvency context.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require the conclusive reliance language. This is standard form and should be non-negotiable.

Deviation 3: Definition of "Entitlement Order" — Narrow Scope
Section Reference: Draft ACA §1.1, "Entitlement Order"
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §2.4 — "Entitlement Order" must encompass all forms of instructions for disposition, whether denominated as entitlement orders, instructions, or otherwise.
Counterparty Draft: Limits "Entitlement Order" to a "notification communicated to the Bank directing the transfer or redemption of a financial asset." This could be read to exclude instructions relating to deposit accounts or commodity accounts, or to exclude general instructions about the disposition of funds.
Risk Rating: MODERATE
Risk Analysis: A narrow definition of "Entitlement Order" could create ambiguity about which instructions the Bank is obligated to follow, potentially allowing the Bank to refuse instructions relating to deposit account funds or commodity positions. In a default, the Secured Party may need to issue both an "entitlement order" and an "instruction," creating procedural uncertainty.
Exposure: Uncertain; primarily operational risk in enforcement.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require the broad Playbook definition.

Deviation 4: Definition of "Financial Asset" — Missing Definition
Section Reference: Draft ACA §1.1 — No definition of "Financial Asset"
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §2.5 — Must include a defined term "Financial Asset" incorporating UCC § 8-102(a)(9).
Counterparty Draft: Omits the defined term entirely.
Risk Rating: MODERATE
Risk Analysis: Without a definition of "Financial Asset," the scope of the security interest in securities and investment property held in the accounts may be ambiguous, potentially creating litigation risk regarding whether specific asset types are covered.
Exposure: Potential loss of priority or perfection as to certain asset types.
Recommended Position: ACCEPT WITH INSERTION — Insert the Playbook definition.

───

B. SECTION 2.1 — GRANTOR'S REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

Deviation 5: Ownership Representation — Diluted
Section Reference: Draft ACA §2.1(a)
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.1 — Grantor must represent it is the sole legal and beneficial owner of all assets credited to the Accounts, free and clear of all liens, claims, and encumbrances (other than the security interest).
Counterparty Draft: Uses the weaker formulation "holds" the Accounts "free and clear of all liens... claims... encumbrances and other rights of third parties whatsoever." The use of "holds" rather than "is the sole legal and beneficial owner" is substantively weaker and could be read narrowly.
Risk Rating: LOW-MODERATE
Risk Analysis: The distinction is primarily drafting; however, in an enforcement scenario, a weak ownership representation could give the Grantor or third parties grounds to contest the scope of the collateral.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require the Playbook formulation.

Deviation 6: No Conflict Representation — Materially Narrowed
Section Reference: Draft ACA §2.1(c)
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.2 — Must include full no-conflict representation covering law, organizational documents, material agreements, and creation of liens.
Counterparty Draft: Only states that execution does not "conflict with or constitute a breach of... the Grantor's organizational documents or any agreement to which the Grantor is a party." This is materially narrower than the Playbook and omits the representation regarding no violation of law and no creation of unintended liens.
Risk Rating: MODERATE
Risk Analysis: Without the full no-conflict language, the Secured Party loses a significant allocution for the Grantor's compliance with law and the absence of other liens. This could weaken enforcement in a workout scenario.
Recommended Position: ACCEPT — This is a modest weakening; the Credit Agreement already contains the full no-conflict representation, so the ACA representation is largely duplicative.

───

C. SECTION 2.2 — BANK'S REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

Deviation 7: Bank's Account Maintenance Representation — Materially Narrowed
Section Reference: Draft ACA §2.2(c)
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.7 — Bank must represent that each Account "is and will remain" a securities/deposit/commodity account under the UCC and that the Bank has no setoff right, lien, or other adverse claim.
Counterparty Draft: Only represents that the Bank "maintains" the accounts and that account numbers/types are accurate. Omits the ongoing "is and will remain" language and the adverse claim/waiver representation.
Risk Rating: HIGH
Risk Analysis: The "is and will remain" language is critical to establishing that the Secured Party continues to have control and that the accounts remain subject to the UCC framework as the transaction progresses. The omission of the adverse claim representation means the Bank has not confirmed the absence of setoff rights, liens, or other claims that could compete with the Secured Party's interest.
Exposure: Potential for the Bank to assert setoff rights or competing liens that the Secured Party did not anticipate, with direct loss to the collateral pool.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require the Playbook representation.

Deviation 8: No Other Control Agreement — Missing
Section Reference: Draft ACA §2.2(d)
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §3.8 — Bank must commit not to enter into any other control agreement or comply with instructions from any other person.
Counterparty Draft: Merely represents that it has not entered into "any other agreement... that could conflict with the Secured Party's rights." This is a backward-looking representation but lacks the forward-looking covenant not to enter into future competing arrangements.
Risk Rating: HIGH
Risk Analysis: Without a forward-looking covenant, the Bank could later enter into a competing control agreement or other arrangement (e.g., a custody agreement or deposit account control agreement with a different secured party) that dilutes the Secured Party's control and perfection. This is a fundamental risk to priority.
Exposure: Priority risk on the full value of the collateral accounts.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require the Playbook's forward-looking covenant.

───

D. SECTION 3 — BANK'S COVENANTS

Deviation 9: Compliance with Instructions — No Explicit Promptness
Section Reference: Draft ACA §3.1
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §4.1 — Bank must comply with Entitlement Orders "promptly" and without duty to inquire.
Counterparty Draft: Requires the Bank to "comply with" Entitlement Orders but does not specify a timetable. Combined with the absence of conclusive reliance protection, this creates delay risk.
Risk Rating: MODERATE
Risk Analysis: In a default scenario, every day of delay in liquidating the collateral increases the risk of market loss. Without an explicit promptness obligation, the Bank could arguably take several business days to process instructions.
Exposure: Market fluctuation risk on the value of securities in the accounts.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Insert "promptly" and the no-inquiry language.

Deviation 10: Statements and Confirmations — Reduced Frequency
Section Reference: Draft ACA §3.4
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §4.4 — Bank must provide monthly statements (minimum) and access to transaction activity, plus prompt notice of unauthorized activity.
Counterparty Draft: Requires statements "at such times as are provided under the applicable account agreement," a standard that may be less frequent than monthly and provides no assurance of access to real-time data.
Risk Rating: LOW-MODERATE
Risk Analysis: The Secured Party needs current information about account balances and activity to monitor collateral coverage in real time. Reduced reporting could mask unauthorized dispositions or declining collateral values.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require monthly statements and electronic access.

Deviation 11: Waiver of Setoff and Liens — Diluted with Exception
Section Reference: Draft ACA §3.7
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §4.7 — Unconditional waiver of setoff, banker's lien, and similar rights.
Counterparty Draft: Contains the waiver but qualifies it with "provided, however, that the Bank retains its right to deduct customary fees and service charges." While the fee carve-out is customary, the Playbook's version permits this carve-out; however, the counterparty's language is ambiguous about whether the carve-out is limited to fees that have accrued and are due.
Risk Rating: LOW
Recommended Position: ACCEPT with clarification — confirm that the fee carve-out applies only to amounts past due and owed under the applicable account agreement.

Deviation 12: Third-Party Instructions — No Obligation to Notify Secured Party
Section Reference: Draft ACA §3.8
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §4.8 — Bank must not comply with instructions from any person other than the Secured Party, and must give prompt notice of any competing instructions.
Counterparty Draft: States the Bank "shall not comply with" instructions from third parties but does not include the playbook's requirement to notify the Secured Party of competing instructions (e.g., from a receiver, trustee, or other creditor).
Risk Rating: MODERATE
Risk Analysis: In an insolvency scenario, a receiver or trustee may seek to direct the Bank. Without a notice obligation, the Secured Party may not learn of competing claims until after action has been taken. Notice allows the Secured Party to intervene promptly.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Insert the notice obligation.

───

E. SECTION 5 — REMEDIES

Deviation 13: Remedies — No Explicit No-Consent and No-Liability Language
Section Reference: Draft ACA §5.1
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §6.1 — Following a default, the Bank must act on the Secured Party's directions without requiring the Grantor's consent, signature, or confirmation, and the Bank is protected from liability for acting on such directions.
Counterparty Draft: Lists the Secured Party's rights to transfer, sell, and execute documents, but does not include the explicit statement that the Bank must comply "without notice to, or consent of, the Grantor" and that the Bank "shall not require the Grantor's signature."
Risk Rating: HIGH
Risk Analysis: This is a material deficiency. Without the explicit no-consent/no-signature language, the Bank could insist on the Grantor's signature before transferring assets, creating significant delay in enforcement and potentially frustrating the Secured Party's ability to liquidate collateral promptly. This strikes at the heart of the control arrangement.
Exposure: Delay in liquidation could result in loss of collateral value and could create grounds for the Grantor or a bankruptcy trustee to challenge the priority or enforceability of the security interest.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require the Playbook language unchanged.

Deviation 14: Grantor's Waiver of Notice — Noncommittal Language
Section Reference: Draft ACA §5.3
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §6.2 — Irrevocable waiver by the Grantor of notice before exercise of remedies.
Counterparty Draft: Uses the passive formulation "The Grantor waives any right to notice prior to any action." While functionally similar, the absence of "irrevocably" could create ambiguity in an enforcement context.
Risk Rating: LOW
Recommended Position: ACCEPT — The waiver is substantively identical; the absence of "irrevocably" is a drafting nuance with limited practical effect.

───

F. SECTION 6 — INDEMNIFICATION

Deviation 15: Bank's Indemnification — Materially Narrowed
Section Reference: Draft ACA §6.1
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §7.1 — Bank indemnifies the Secured Party for (i) failure to comply with the Agreement, (ii) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (iii) actions taken in accordance with court orders that cause loss, and (iv) claims by third parties relating to the Bank's actions under the Agreement.
Counterparty Draft: Limits the Bank's indemnity to losses arising from "gross negligence or willful misconduct" only. This omits the Bank's obligation to indemnify for simple breach of the Agreement, actions taken under court orders, and third-party claims.
Risk Rating: HIGH
Risk Analysis: By limiting the Bank's indemnity to gross negligence/willful misconduct, the counterparty eliminates the Bank's liability for ordinary negligence or simple breach of contract. In a control agreement context, the Bank's primary obligation is compliance with instructions; if the Bank is only liable for gross negligence/willful misconduct, the Secured Party has significantly less protection if the Bank fails to execute instructions in a timely or correct manner without rising to the level of gross negligence.
Exposure: The value of the collateral that could be lost or impaired due to the Bank's failure to comply.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require the full Playbook indemnification.

Deviation 16: Secured Party's Indemnification — Missing Exclusions
Section Reference: Draft ACA §6.3
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §7.3 — Secured Party's indemnification to the Bank excludes losses from the Bank's breach, violation of law, or compliance with third-party instructions.
Counterparty Draft: Contains a broad indemnification of the Bank with no exclusions.
Risk Rating: MODERATE
Risk Analysis: The absence of exclusions exposes the Secured Party to potential indemnification liability for the Bank's own failures, including the Bank's breach of the Agreement or compliance with instructions from unauthorized parties.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require the Playbook exclusions.

───

G. SECTION 7 — MISCELLANEOUS

Deviation 17: Governing Law — Non-New York
Section Reference: Draft ACA §7.4
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §8.4 — New York governing law with specific UCC perfection provisions.
Counterparty Draft: Governed by "the laws of the State of [●]" without specifying New York and without the refinements for UCC perfection.
Risk Rating: HIGH
Risk Analysis: New York governing law is the firm standard for secured finance transactions and provides a well-developed body of beneficial case law on UCC Article 8 and 9 matters, including control agreements. Using another jurisdiction's law creates uncertainty and could materially affect the interpretation of control and perfection provisions. Additionally, the specific acknowledgment of the UCC perfection provisions is critical to ensuring the security interest is properly perfected.
Exposure: Potential loss of perfected status or enforcement uncertainty.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require New York governing law and the UCC perfection language.

Deviation 18: Jurisdiction and Waiver of Jury Trial — Non-Exclusive, No Jury Waiver
Section Reference: Draft ACA §7.5
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §8.5 — Exclusive New York forum and express jury trial waiver.
Counterparty Draft: Uses nonexclusive jurisdiction and omits the jury trial waiver.
Risk Rating: MODERATE
Risk Analysis: Nonexclusive jurisdiction creates uncertainty about the forum for disputes. More importantly, the absence of a jury trial waiver exposes the Secured Party to the risk of a jury in any enforcement action, which is generally viewed as adverse to sophisticated financial parties. In an enforcement context, an unfavorable jury finding could materially impair recovery.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require exclusive New York forum and jury trial waiver.

Deviation 19: Termination — No Written Release Requirement
Section Reference: Draft ACA §7.15
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §8.15 — Termination requires the Secured Party's written release; no automatic termination.
Counterparty Draft: Provides that the Agreement "shall terminate upon the indefeasible payment in full of the Secured Obligations and the release of the security interest in the Accounts." This is a standard formulation but does not expressly require the Secured Party's written release to the Bank and could be read to allow automatic termination upon payment.
Risk Rating: MODERATE
Risk Analysis: Automatic termination could create a gap between the time the Secured Obligations are repaid and the time the Bank receives clear direction. During such gap, the Bank might reasonably refuse to act on the Secured Party's instructions because the Agreement has arguably terminated. Conversely, automatic termination could give the Grantor a basis to argue the Bank was no longer obligated to follow the Secured Party's instructions.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Require the Secured Party's written release as the exclusive termination mechanism.

───

H. OTHER MISSING PROTECTIONS

Deviation 20: No-Action Instruction — No Definition or Procedural Clarity
Section Reference: Draft ACA §1.1
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §2.2
Counterparty Draft: Defines "No-Action Instruction" but does not specify the procedure for delivery or the effect on the Bank's obligations.
Risk Rating: LOW
Recommended Position: ACCEPT with clarification — confirm the procedural mechanics by agreement among counsel.

Deviation 21: Successorship of Secured Party — Missing Assignment Provision
Section Reference: Draft ACA §7.3
Playbook Requirement: Playbook §8.3 — Right of successor agent assignment without consent.
Counterparty Draft: General successors and assigns provision that does not expressly permit the Secured Party to assign this Agreement to a successor administrative agent without the consent of the other parties.
Risk Rating: MODERATE
Risk Analysis: In a refinancing or agency succession, the new agent may need to receive the benefit of the control arrangement. Without an express assignment provision, the Grantor or the Bank could resist the assignment, requiring the execution of a new ACA.
Recommended Position: REJECT — Insert the Playbook provision.

VI. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS

1. Submit the Redline to the counterparty with a cover note emphasizing that Items #1, #7, #8, #13, #15, #17, #18, and #19 are non-negotiable and must be conformed to the Playbook.

2. For the remaining REJECT items (#2, #3, #9, #10, #12, #16, #21), be prepared to negotiate in exchange for reasonable commercial accommodations in other areas (e.g., fee bifurcation, transition periods, or notice periods).

3. Confirm with the Depository Bank that it will sign the ACA as revised. If the Bank declines any required provision (e.g., expanded indemnification), escalate to senior counsel and evaluate whether an alternative depository bank is practicable before the closing deadline.

4. Coordinate with local counsel to confirm that the perfection analysis under the UCC (particularly with respect to the choice of governing law) is correct for each collateral account's jurisdiction.

5. Following execution, ensure that (i) the Bank acknowledges in writing the accuracy of each account detail on Schedule I, and (ii) a copy of the executed ACA is filed with the closing documents and registered in the firm's document management system.
